DELIVERABLE: `lib/preferences/vocabulary.ts` + `__tests__/preferences-vocabulary.test.ts` + a commit.

=== WHAT THIS IS ===
A per-instructor preference memory feature stores atomic records about how an instructor assesses. This module defines the CLOSED set of predicates that may ever be stored, and the validation schema for extraction candidates. Nothing outside this list is storable.

=== THE VOCABULARY (exactly these eight, no more) ===
| predicate | value type | affectsScore |
|---|---|---|
| `grading.partial_credit_mode` | enum: `none` \| `fixed_levels` \| `continuous_range` \| `elementwise` \| `pass_fail` | true |
| `grading.score_precision` | number | true |
| `grading.criterion_weighting` | enum: `equal` \| `custom` | true |
| `grading.edge_case_rule` | free text | true |
| `feedback.granularity` | enum: `overall` \| `criterion` \| `both` | false |
| `feedback.length` | enum: `brief` \| `moderate` \| `detailed` | false |
| `feedback.orientation` | enum: `verdict` \| `corrective` \| `actionable` | false |
| `feedback.register` | enum: `plain` \| `formal` \| `disciplinary` | false |

Export the predicate keys as a closed TypeScript union type (not `string`), plus a table carrying value type, `affectsScore`, and the allowed enum values.

=== THE CANDIDATE RECORD SCHEMA (Zod) ===
A candidate proposed by an extractor must validate against a Zod schema with these fields:
- `predicate` — must be one of the eight; anything else is rejected
- `value` — must match that predicate's declared value type and enum set
- `valueText` — the natural-language rendering, Korean
- `evidence` — object: `sourceTable` (`bulk_grading_messages` | `grading_chats` | `derived_criteria`), `refId` (uuid), `span` (tuple of two non-negative integers, start < end), `quote` (non-empty string)
- `commitment` — enum: `asserted` | `tentative` | `hypothetical` | `reported` | `negated`
- `isExplicit` — boolean

`zod` is ALREADY a dependency in `package.json` — do not add it, do not add anything else.

=== DO NOT DEFINE THESE (deliberately excluded during design) ===
- Any `authoring.*` predicate — the signal to observe them does not exist in this schema yet.
- `grading.rubric_mode` — there is no instructor-authored analytic rubric UI in this product.
- `grading.late_policy`, `grading.requirement_penalty_policy` — no late/format penalty feature exists.
- Any `operations.*` predicate — no anonymous grading, no moderation, no resubmission feature.
- Any free-form "grading philosophy" field. The vocabulary is closed on purpose.
- Any predicate expressing instructor strictness or leniency as a scalar. That confounds task difficulty, cohort, and rubric design, and must never be modelled.

=== TESTS (tests-after is fine here; this is new code with no existing behavior to pin) ===
`__tests__/preferences-vocabulary.test.ts` must assert:
(i) a candidate with a predicate outside the eight is REJECTED by the schema;
(ii) `affectsScore` is true for every `grading.*` and false for every `feedback.*`;
(iii) an enum-typed predicate rejects a value outside its allowed set;
(iv) `grading.score_precision` accepts a number and rejects a string;
(v) an evidence span with `start >= end` is rejected, and a negative offset is rejected;
(vi) an empty `quote` is rejected.
Follow the existing test style in `__tests__/prompts.test.ts`.

=== VERIFY (paste real output) ===
1. `npx vitest run __tests__/preferences-vocabulary.test.ts`
2. `npx tsc --noEmit`
3. `npm run lint`
4. `git status --short`
5. `git diff --stat origin/staging -- package.json` — MUST be empty (proves no dependency was added)

=== MANUAL-QA (required) ===
Write a throwaway script under `/tmp` that imports nothing from the app but prints, for each of the eight predicates, the result of running your schema against (a) one valid candidate and (b) one deliberately invalid candidate. Run it with `npx tsx` or compile-free equivalent and paste the 16 results. Binary observable: all eight valid ones parse, all eight invalid ones fail. Delete the script and paste the `rm` receipt.

=== ADVERSARIAL CLASSES ===
- malformed_input: this module IS the malformed-input gate — assertions (i), (iii), (iv), (v), (vi) are the probe. Report each result.
- prompt_injection: a candidate whose `quote` contains text like "ignore previous instructions" must still be treated as ordinary data — confirm the schema neither executes nor special-cases it.
- misleading_success_output: paste real command output.

+import { z } from "zod";
+
+/**
+ * Closed predicate vocabulary for instructor preference memory.
+ * These eight predicates are the only storable observations about how an instructor assesses.
+ */
+
+export type Predicate =
+  | "grading.partial_credit_mode"
+  | "grading.score_precision"
+  | "grading.criterion_weighting"
+  | "grading.edge_case_rule"
+  | "feedback.granularity"
+  | "feedback.length"
+  | "feedback.orientation"
+  | "feedback.register";
+
+export const PREDICATES: Predicate[] = [
+  "grading.partial_credit_mode",
+  "grading.score_precision",
+  "grading.criterion_weighting",
+  "grading.edge_case_rule",
+  "feedback.granularity",
+  "feedback.length",
+  "feedback.orientation",
+  "feedback.register",
+];
+
+export const PREDICATE_SET = new Set(PREDICATES);
+
+/**
+ * Metadata table for each predicate.
+ * Carries value type, affectsScore flag, and allowed enum values (if applicable).
+ */
+export interface PredicateMetadata {
+  predicate: Predicate;
+  valueType: "enum" | "number" | "text";
+  affectsScore: boolean;
+  allowedValues?: string[];
+}
+
+export const PREDICATE_TABLE: Record<Predicate, PredicateMetadata> = {
+  "grading.partial_credit_mode": {
+    predicate: "grading.partial_credit_mode",
+    valueType: "enum",
+    affectsScore: true,
+    allowedValues: ["none", "fixed_levels", "continuous_range", "elementwise", "pass_fail"],
+  },
+  "grading.score_precision": {
+    predicate: "grading.score_precision",
+    valueType: "number",
+    affectsScore: true,
+  },
+  "grading.criterion_weighting": {
+    predicate: "grading.criterion_weighting",
+    valueType: "enum",
+    affectsScore: true,
+    allowedValues: ["equal", "custom"],
+  },
+  "grading.edge_case_rule": {
+    predicate: "grading.edge_case_rule",
+    valueType: "text",
+    affectsScore: true,
+  },
+  "feedback.granularity": {
+    predicate: "feedback.granularity",
+    valueType: "enum",
+    affectsScore: false,
+    allowedValues: ["overall", "criterion", "both"],
+  },
+  "feedback.length": {
+    predicate: "feedback.length",
+    valueType: "enum",
+    affectsScore: false,
+    allowedValues: ["brief", "moderate", "detailed"],
+  },
+  "feedback.orientation": {

+    valueType: "enum",
+    affectsScore: false,
+    allowedValues: ["verdict", "corrective", "actionable"],
+  },
+  "feedback.register": {
+    predicate: "feedback.register",
+    valueType: "enum",
+    affectsScore: false,
+    allowedValues: ["plain", "formal", "disciplinary"],
+  },
+};
+
+/**
+ * Value type schemas for each predicate.
+ * Maps predicate to its Zod validator.
+ */
+const createValueSchema = (predicate: Predicate): z.ZodType => {
+  const meta = PREDICATE_TABLE[predicate];
+
+  if (meta.valueType === "enum" && meta.allowedValues) {
+    return z.enum(meta.allowedValues as [string, ...string[]]);
+  } else if (meta.valueType === "number") {
+    return z.number();
+  } else if (meta.valueType === "text") {
+    return z.string();
+  }
+
+  throw new Error(`Unknown value type for predicate ${predicate}`);
+};
+
+/**
+ * Evidence object schema: sourceTable, refId, span, quote.

+  sourceTable: z.enum(["bulk_grading_messages", "grading_chats", "derived_criteria"]),
+  refId: z.string().uuid(),
+  span: z.tuple([z.number().nonnegative(), z.number().nonnegative()]).refine(
+    ([start, end]) => start < end,
+    {
+      message: "span start must be less than end",
+    }
+  ),
+  quote: z.string().min(1, "quote must not be empty"),
+});
+
+export type Evidence = z.infer<typeof evidenceSchema>;
+
+/**

+ */
+export const commitmentSchema = z.enum(["asserted", "tentative", "hypothetical", "reported", "negated"]);
+export type Commitment = z.infer<typeof commitmentSchema>;
+
+/**
